topics.topic: Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026
topics.why_in_news: Government operationalised the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 through Online Gaming Rules, 2026 to regulate digital gaming ecosystem, prohibit online money gaming and promote e-sports.
prelims_quick_notes: Betting and gambling fall under Entry 34 of State List.
Online gaming transcends state boundaries requiring central digital regulation.
Online Gaming Authority of India (OGAI) established under MeitY.
Online money games completely prohibited under new framework.
E-sports recognised as skill-based competitive gaming activity.
Rules provide registration and regulatory framework for gaming platforms.
Mandatory age verification and user protection safeguards introduced.
Rules aim to balance innovation, digital economy growth and consumer protection.
important_facts: Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act enacted in 2025.
Rules come into force from 1 May 2026.
OGAI functions under Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
Registration validity for gaming platforms up to 10 years.
Section 69A of IT Act empowers blocking of illegal apps/websites.
Offences related to online money gaming are cognisable and non-bailable.
Mobile gaming forms nearly 90% of gaming ecosystem.
key_provisions: Classification of games into e-sports, online social games and online money games.
Ban on offering, advertising and facilitating online money gaming.
Financial institutions prohibited from processing related transactions.
Appeal mechanism to OGAI and Secretary, MeitY.
Mandatory parental controls and addiction safeguards.
Digital compliance and public disclosure framework introduced.
exam_relevance: Important for Polity, Governance and Digital Regulation.
Useful for federalism, platform governance and digital economy topics.
Can be linked with Article 21, data privacy and emerging technologies.
prelims_traps: Betting and gambling fall under State List, not Union List.
Online money games prohibited irrespective of skill versus chance distinction.
OGAI functions under MeitY, not Ministry of Home Affairs.
